subject: math
title: Subtract Multiples of 10 (Grade 1)
seo_title: Grade 1 Subtracting Tens Worksheets: Subtract Multiples of 10 Like 70 − 30 With Rods and Number Lines
domain: Number and Operations in Base Ten
standard_text: Subtract multiples of 10 in the range 10-90 from multiples of 10 in the range 10-90 (positive or zero differences), using concrete models or drawings and strategies based on place value, properties of operations, and/or the relationship between addition and subtraction; relate the strategy to a written method and explain the reasoning used.
meta_desc: Free Grade 1 worksheets for subtracting multiples of 10, like 70 − 30 and 90 − 50: take away ten rods, tens facts, count back on a number line, think addition, missing numbers and word problems with dimes. 100 practice questions with an answer key.
key_big: Subtract tens like ones: 7 tens − 3 tens = 4 tens, so 70 − 30 = 40.
key_sub: Use a fact you know (7 − 3 = 4), then write the 0, because the answer counts tens. Check by adding: 40 + 30 = 70.
body_html:
Take away tens like ones

70 is 7 tens. 30 is 3 tens. To find 70 − 30, take away 3 tens. You know 7 − 3 = 4. So 7 tens − 3 tens = 4 tens. That is 40.

Use a fact you know

What is 90 − 50?

9 − 5 = 4. So 9 tens − 5 tens = 4 tens.

Answer: 40

Count back by tens

On a number line, jump back 10 at a time. Count the jumps.

Think addition

Subtraction and addition go together. To find 80 − 50, ask: 50 + what makes 80? Count up by tens: 60, 70, 80. That is 3 tens.

Missing number

80 − ☐ = 50

Think: 50 + ☐ = 80. 50 + 30 = 80.

Answer: 30

Word problem

Leo has 6 dimes. That is 60¢. He spends 20¢. How much is left?

60¢ − 20¢ = 40¢. 6 dimes take away 2 dimes is 4 dimes.

Answer: 40¢

Common mistakes

MistakeWhat to do instead
70 − 30 = 4 (the 0 is lost)4 tens is 40. Write the 0
70 − 30 = 67 (took away 3 ones)30 is 3 tens. Take away 3 tens
70 − 30 = 100 (added)Take away means count back
80 − ☐ = 50, writing 130Think 50 + ☐ = 80. The box is 30

faq.q: How do you subtract multiples of 10 in 1st grade?
faq.a: Think of each number as tens. 70 − 30 is 7 tens − 3 tens = 4 tens, so the answer is 40. Children use the fact 7 − 3 = 4 they already know.
They did 7 − 3 and forgot that the answer counts tens. Ask “4 what?” 4 tens is 40, so write the 0.
It is the Common Core standard for Grade 1: subtract multiples of 10 from 10 to 90, like 60 − 20, using models, place value and the link between addition and subtraction.

faq.q: How can I help my child practice subtracting tens at home?
faq.a: Use dimes or bundles of 10 straws. Show 8 bundles, take away 3, and count the tens left. Then write it as 80 − 30 = 50.

items.e: Count the tens like ones. 3 − 1 = 2. So 3 tens − 1 ten = 2 tens.

items.q: 5 tens − 3 tens = ?

sets.title: Count back on a number line

items.q: Start at 40. Jump back by tens. What is 40 − 20?
items.e: Start at 40. Make 2 jumps back: 30, 20. You land on 20.

items.q: Start at 40. Jump back by tens. What is 40 − 30?
items.e: Start at 40. Make 3 jumps back: 30, 20, 10. You land on 10.

items.q: Count back by tens: 30, 20, ☐. What number goes in the box?
items.e: Each step back takes away 10: 30, 20, 10. The box is 10. So 30 − 20 = 10.

items.q: Start at 40. Jump back by tens. What is 40 − 10?
items.e: Start at 40. Make 1 jump back: 30. You land on 30.

items.q: Start at 90. Jump back by tens. What is 90 − 10?

items.q: Which subtraction does the number line show?
items.e: It starts at 50. There are 2 jumps of 10. That is 20. 50 − 20 = 30.

items.q: Start at the dot. Count back 6 tens. Where do you land?

items.q: Start at 70. Jump back 50 in one jump. Where do you land?

items.q: Which addition fact checks 90 − 10 = 80?
items.e: Add the answer and the part you took away. 80 + 10 = 90. You get back to 90, so 90 − 10 = 80 is right.
Count up from 10 to 20 by tens. 10 + 10 = 20. So 20 − 10 = 10.

items.q: 70 − ☐ = 30. What number goes in the box?
items.e: Think addition: 30 + ☐ = 70. 30 + 40 = 70. So 70 − 40 = 30. The box is 40.

items.q: Leo says 70 − 30 = 4. That is not right. What is 70 − 30?
items.e: He forgot the 0. 4 tens is 40, not 4. 70 − 30 = 40. Check: 40 + 30 = 70.

items.e: Think addition: 60 + ☐ = 80. 60 + 20 = 80. So 80 − 20 = 60. The box is 20.

items.e: Add the answer and the part you took away. 10 + 60 = 70. You get back to 70, so 70 − 60 = 10 is right.

items.q: 40 − ☐ = 30. What number goes in the box?
items.e: Think addition: 30 + ☐ = 40. 30 + 10 = 40. So 40 − 10 = 30. The box is 10.

items.e: She took away 5 ones. But 50 is 5 tens, so take away 5 tens. 80 − 50 = 30. Check: 30 + 50 = 80.

items.q: Emma says 60 − 20 = 80. That is not right. What is 60 − 20?
items.e: She added. To take away, count back 2 tens from 60. 60 − 20 = 40. Check: 40 + 20 = 60.

items.q: 90 − ☐ = 70. What number goes in the box?

items.q: Mia has 60 beads. She uses 20 beads. How many beads are left?
items.e: Take away: 60 − 20 = 40. Mia has 40 beads left.

items.q: There are 30 ducks in a pond. 10 ducks fly away. How many ducks are left?
items.e: 30 − 10 = 20. 20 ducks are left.

items.q: Sam has 8 bags of beads. Each bag has 10 beads. He gives away 3 bags. How many beads does he have now?
items.e: 8 bags = 80 beads. 3 bags = 30 beads. 80 − 30 = 50. Watch out: 5 is the number of bags, not beads.

items.q: A box has 40 crayons. 10 crayons are broken. How many crayons are not broken?
items.e: 40 − 10 = 30. 30 crayons are not broken.

items.q: Noah has these dimes. A dime is 10¢. He spends 30¢. How much money is left?
items.e: Count the dimes by tens: 7 dimes = 70¢. 70¢ − 30¢ = 40¢.

items.q: A book has 90 pages. Nora has read 40 pages. How many pages are left to read?
items.e: 90 − 40 = 50. Nora has 50 pages left to read.

items.q: Stickers come in sheets of 10. Kai has 6 sheets. He uses 4 sheets. How many stickers are left?
items.e: 6 sheets = 60 stickers. 4 sheets = 40 stickers. 60 − 40 = 20. 2 is the number of sheets left, not stickers.

items.q: There are 50 kids on the playground. 20 kids go inside. How many kids are still outside?
items.e: 50 − 20 = 30. 30 kids are still outside.

items.q: Eli has 90¢. A toy car costs 60¢. He buys it. How much money does he have left?
items.e: 90¢ − 60¢ = 30¢. Think: 9 dimes take away 6 dimes is 3 dimes.

items.q: A farm has 80 chickens. 50 chickens are in the barn. The rest are outside. How many chickens are outside?
Grace has 80 blocks. Lily has 30 blocks. How many more blocks does Grace have than Lily?
items.e: Find the difference. 80 − 30 = 50. Grace has 50 more blocks.

items.q: Luis has these dimes. He buys a ball for 50¢. How much money is left?
A baker makes 60 muffins. 30 muffins are sold. How many muffins are left?
items.e: 60 − 30 = 30. 30 muffins are left.

items.q: Owen needs 70 points to win. He has 40 points. How many more points does he need?
items.e: Think: 40 + ☐ = 70. Count up by tens: 50, 60, 70. That is 3 tens. Owen needs 30 more points.

items.q: There are 90 chairs in the gym. Kids sit in 70 chairs. How many chairs are empty?
items.e: 90 − 70 = 20. 20 chairs are empty.

items.q: Zoe picks 50 apples. She puts 10 apples in each bag. She gives away 2 bags. How many apples are left?
Omar has 20 toy cars. Ava has 60 toy cars. How many fewer cars does Omar have than Ava?
items.e: Compare. Take the smaller number from the bigger one: 60 − 20 = 40. Omar has 40 fewer cars.

items.q: There are 70 books on a shelf. Kids take 60 books. How many books are on the shelf now?
items.e: 70 − 60 = 10. 7 tens take away 6 tens is 1 ten. 10 books are left.

items.q: Jack has 40¢. He gets 3 more dimes. Then he spends 50¢. How much money is left?
Ben had some marbles. He lost 20 marbles. Now he has 50 marbles. How many marbles did he have at first?
items.e: Put the lost marbles back. 50 + 20 = 70. Check: 70 − 20 = 50. Do not subtract 50 − 20 here.
